espn-603998.headline: England defend their coach; Australia argue about pay
beats: England's players have denied rumours of a rift and say they will fight to protect Steve Borthwick, whose bosses have given him their full support. Australia arrive in London in the middle of a pay dispute.

Ugo Monye thinks the siege mentality suits England. Their best Six Nations performance was the 46–48 loss to France. Maro Itoje, captain again after missing the summer Tests, has to stop the ill discipline that has crept in of late.
Australia conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October, and lost 25–7 away to England on 1 November 2025. Win anyway and they go up to fifth, with England down to seventh.
Fraser McReight wins his 50th cap in the middle of it all. A week later England host Japan and Australia go to Scotland, both hoping the news by then is about rugby.

espn-603999.headline: South Africa beat New Zealand thrice. France can undo it
beats: South Africa beat New Zealand three times in a fortnight, the last 43–28, and have been first in the world rankings since 31 August. Lose in Saint-Denis and they drop to second, behind New Zealand.
France lost 17–32 at home to South Africa on 8 November 2025. In the Championship they have since lost only to New Zealand, 32–34, and arrive on three straight wins.

South Africa led Italy 45–0 after half an hour and won 66–7. Rassie Erasmus summed it up as "It wasn’t perfect, but it was proper." He also said they must play much better to be competitive against France.

Ireland follow on 21 November. Victor Matfield would not be surprised if Erasmus picks uncapped youngsters for one of these games. That is a brave thing to try against a France side that has scored 42 or more three times running.

espn-604000.headline: Someone in Genova has to remember how to win
beats: Italy have lost five straight. They conceded 66, 57 and 47 in their last three Championship games, the latest a nine-try defeat to South Africa in Turin. Argentina have won once all year.

Argentina's last outing was a 12–42 loss in Ireland. Their best result since July is a 28–28 draw with Australia, which says less about attack than about how rarely they have finished a game in front.
Win and Italy go up to 9th in the world, above Fiji and Wales, on the strength of one evening.
A week later Italy host Fiji, who also have no points. Argentina go to France, which is not where anyone goes to find form.

espn-604001.headline: Wales held off Japan on the line. Now New Zealand
beats: New Zealand have scored 50, 43 and 43 in their last three Tests, the latest a 43–21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield. Wales beat Japan 28–21 in Cardiff the same day, and needed a desperate defensive stand in the final moments to stop Japan scoring the equaliser.

Steve Tandy blamed rust from a first Test since July and admitted, "I thought we’d be better." That July game was a 43–0 defeat in South Africa. Wales lost 26–52 at home to New Zealand in November 2025.
Beauden Barrett scored twice at Murrayfield. He is 35 and has 50 Test tries in 148 caps. A Wales win would lift them above Fiji to ninth in the world, and New Zealand would still be second.
Wales host Australia a week later, two points ahead of them in the table. That is the game Wales will have been counting on.

espn-604002.headline: Wales blamed rust. England have had longer to gather it
beats: Japan carried 82 times to Wales' 54 in Cardiff on 7 November and made them tackle 235 times. They still lost 28–21, held up at the line in the final moments of a game they controlled for long stretches.
Steve Tandy put Wales' flat patches down to their first Test since July: "it does get clunky". England have not played since beating Argentina 31–24 on 18 July.
A Japan win would drop England to 7th in the world, below Scotland and Australia, the week before they host New Zealand.
Japan's last two defeats were by six and seven points. Close has become a habit. It has not yet become a win.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland can win this by fifty and gain nothing
beats: Ireland are third in the world, and the rankings only move one way in Dublin. A draw would drop them below France. Fiji arrive with four defeats from four in the Nations Championship, the last a 54–17 loss in France on 7 November.
Ireland scored six tries against Argentina, three of them by Hugo Keenan, and won 42–12. Andy Farrell and Tadhg Beirne still said they could have been more ruthless. Fiji have just let in 54.

Rassie Erasmus says South Africa have to play much better against France and Ireland. Ireland host them on 21 November. Fiji go to Italy that day, and Italy are the only other side in the competition without a point.
So both teams have their real Test next week. Only one of them can afford to treat this as a rehearsal.

espn-604004.headline: Both lost 21–43 to New Zealand. One gets to forget it
beats: Australia lost 21–43 to New Zealand at home on 17 October, a week after conceding 50 to them. Scotland lost by exactly the same score at Murrayfield on 7 November.
Ewan Ashman scored a hat-trick that day, and Scotland still did not score in the second half. Captain Sione Tuipulotu took "full responsibility" for the collapse.

They sit sixth and seventh in the world, and a Scotland win by any margin takes them up to fifth, above England. Australia have a game in hand in the Nations Championship and, unlike Scotland, a positive points difference.

Gregor Townsend spent a summer in the 1990s playing club rugby for Warringah in Sydney. This fixture has produced some of the best rugby of his nine years in charge. Both sides have just had the same lesson from the same teacher, and Murrayfield finds out who took notes.

espn-604005.headline: England get to test the 'average' All Blacks theory
beats: New Zealand are four from four in the Nations Championship and put 43 past Scotland at Murrayfield on 7 November. Hamish Bidwell still called them "an average All Blacks side" and said someone other than the Springboks would expose them.

England have the best claim to the job. They beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. Their own year is less tidy: beaten by Italy and by France, 46–48, in March, then two wins in July, the last 31–24 in Argentina.
Bidwell's charge sheet includes a backline that kicked good ball away. One of the kickers was Beauden Barrett, 35, who also scored twice in that game and now has 50 Test tries from 148 caps.

England win by 16 or more and they climb to third in the world, above Ireland and France. New Zealand's next fixture is Chile at the 2027 World Cup, which leaves a long time to argue about the theory.

espn-604006.headline: Japan nearly drew in Cardiff. Scotland just shipped 43
beats: Wales needed a desperate rearguard in the final moments to stop Japan scoring an equaliser, and still won only 28–21. Steve Tandy called it a bonus-point win and admitted his side "weren't ruthless enough".
Scotland come off a 21–43 home defeat to New Zealand, over by the 51st minute. It is the same score Ireland put on them in March. Sione Tuipulotu said they were "nowhere near accurate enough".

Scotland sit sixth in the Nations Championship, level on points with England and Wales, and their second halves are the problem. A side that keeps games close is the wrong visitor for that. Even a draw drops Scotland to seventh in the world, below Australia.
Scotland's next fixture is Uruguay at home at the World Cup, in October 2027. That is a long time to sit on a bad afternoon.

espn-604007.headline: Andrew Porter has had a year to think about the scrum
beats: Porter has not played for Ireland since last November, when South Africa's scrum gave him a night he has stewed over ever since. The Leinster loosehead says he is ready to settle the score.
That day in Dublin ended 13–24. Ireland have since put six tries and 42–12 on Argentina, and Andy Farrell's verdict was that they could be "more ruthless".
South Africa scored nine tries against Italy in a 66–7 win. Rassie Erasmus still says they must play much better to be competitive against France and Ireland. That is either modesty or a warning.

The Springboks lead the Nations Championship from New Zealand on points difference alone, and an Ireland win would drop them to second in the world, behind New Zealand. Either way, Porter knows where it starts.

espn-604008.headline: Someone in Udine has to win a game
beats: Italy and Fiji have played eight Nations Championship games between them and won none. Fiji sit 11th of 12, Italy 12th, both still on zero points.

Their last outings were on the same Saturday: a depleted Italy lost 66–7 to South Africa in Turin, and Fiji lost 54–17 to France in Lyon. That is 120 points conceded by two defences that now meet each other.
Fiji at least beat Japan 34–28 in October. Italy have lost five straight, and a win would still lift them to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales.
After this, Italy's next game is South Africa again, at the World Cup. Something to take into that would help.

espn-604009.headline: France need a win and sixteen points to spare
beats: A France win by 16 or more lifts them above Ireland to third in the world. They have scored 42, 42 and 54 in their last three Tests. Argentina conceded 42 in Dublin on 6 November.

That 42–12 loss came with six Irish tries and a pack that never settled. It leaves Argentina on one win from seven this year. Their nearest thing to a result was a 28–28 draw at home to Australia in September.
South Africa are already thinking about France. Rassie Erasmus put 66 on Italy and still said his side "have to play much better than this" to compete with them.
Argentina's hope is the sort of game France played against England in March. France won 48–46, and nobody defended much.

espn-604010.headline: Italy have lost four from four. Wales could still trail them
beats: Wales beat Italy 31-17 in Cardiff in March. Lose to Australia here by any margin and Wales drop below Italy and Japan in the world rankings, twelfth at best.
Australia are not arriving in comfort. They conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October, a fortnight after beating South Africa 42-38. They went into November in a pay dispute.
Wales have their own scar. South Africa held them scoreless in July, 43-0. Steve Tandy called this November pivotal, with Japan first, then New Zealand, then Australia last.
Australia's next fixture is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027. Wales have nothing else scheduled, so whatever happens here is the number they keep.
